## JuliaCon 2026 · short talk

**Let’s run Julia everywhere — from mobile to web**

A Rust-based VM for a subset of Julia, running where the official runtime is hard to deploy.

::: {.notes}
~10 minutes including live demos. Slot is 15 min; leave buffer for Q&A.
:::

## Motivation

Julia’s Tier‑1 platforms cover most users.

But we are greedy: we want more.

- Offline mobile (airplane mode)
- Browsers without long TTFX
- Older ARMv7 devices
- **iOS / iPadOS** (no JIT, strict App Review)

## Why not `libjulia`?

Official Julia leans on **LLVM JIT**.

That is a poor fit when:

- writable+executable memory is banned (iOS)
- cold start / binary size must stay small (web, mobile)
- the host wants a **static** link (Swift / Flutter)

We need a portable runtime that does **not** depend on JIT.

## Approach

**SubsetJuliaVM (sjulia)** — a Rust VM for a strict subset of Julia.

```
Julia source → Parser → Lowering → Compiler → VM
```

- Pure Rust parser / pipeline (no tree-sitter runtime)
- Stack-based bytecode interpreter (**no JIT**)
- Same subset on native, **WASM**, and **iOS**

OSS core: [AtelierArith/julia-vm-oss](https://github.com/AtelierArith/julia-vm-oss)

## Design commitments

1. **Output parity** with upstream Julia (fixtures + oracles)
2. **Upstream-driven** design — read `julia/` before inventing shortcuts
3. **Pure Julia first** for Base/stdlib-shaped code; Rust for no-JIT hot paths

Parity target series: Julia **1.12**

## Where it ships

| Target | How |
|--------|-----|
| Web / education | WASM + browser playground |
| iOS / iPadOS | C ABI → SwiftUI app (App Store) |
| Flutter / mobile | Static link via the same C ABI |
| AoT experiments | Transpile subset Julia → Rust binaries |

## Demo · Plotly via Plots

```{=html}
<div class="sjulia-executor" data-code="using Plots\nx = 0:0.1:2π\nplot(x, sin.(x), label=&quot;sin&quot;)\nplot!(x, cos.(x), label=&quot;cos&quot;)\ntitle!(&quot;in the browser&quot;)"></div>
```

## Demo · Mandelbrot heatmap

```{=html}
<div class="sjulia-executor" data-code="using Plots\nfunction esc(c, n)\n  z = 0.0+0.0im\n  for k in 1:n\n    abs2(z) > 4 && return k\n    z = z^2 + c\n  end; n\nend\nxs = range(-2, 1; length=80)\nys = range(-1.2, 1.2; length=60)\nheatmap(xs, ys, esc.(xs' .+ im .* ys, Ref(40)))"></div>
```

## Beyond the browser

**iOS / iPadOS** — native app, no JIT, App Store compliant

- [SubsetJuliaVM on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/subsetjuliavm/id6757257182)

**Web playground**

- [terasakisatoshi.github.io/subset_julia](https://terasakisatoshi.github.io/subset_julia/)

Static linking also targets Flutter / Swift hosts via the C ABI.

## What about packages?

Not a full Pkg ecosystem — **bundled subsets** for education / demos, with upstream trees as parity oracles, e.g.:

- Plots.jl · Distributions.jl · OrdinaryDiffEq.jl
- Symbolics.jl · DataStructures.jl · Rotations.jl · …

Goal: useful Julia **where Julia normally cannot run**, not a drop-in `libjulia`.

## How it was built

Much of the VM was written with **Claude Code / Codex / Cursor**.

Human role:

- Keep designs aligned with upstream Julia
- Prefer Pure Julia where possible
- Gate correctness with parity fixtures and audits

## Takeaways

- A **no-JIT Rust VM** makes Julia syntax runnable on iOS and the web
- WASM demos (this deck) and App Store apps share one pipeline
- Portable alternative to embedding `libjulia`

**Try it:** [julia-vm-oss](https://github.com/AtelierArith/julia-vm-oss) · [web playground](https://terasakisatoshi.github.io/subset_julia/) · [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/subsetjuliavm/id6757257182)
